title: Preserve leading zeros and literal NA codes
text:
Import CSV and text with confidence This small import fixture is explicitly fictional and separate from the penguin research data. Its IDs contain leading zeros, NA is a literal site code, and MISSING marks one unavailable amount. Encoding, quoting, decimal symbols, and missing-value rules all affect what a reader produces. path = DATA_DIR / "public" / "import_practice_semicolon.csv"
result = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";", comment="#", encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype="string", keep_default_na=False)
print(result)
print("IDs:", result["record_id"].tolist())
print("Site codes:", result["site_code"].tolist()) Read the fixture again with record_id and site_code as strings, comma decimal symbols for amount_eur, and only MISSING in amount_eur treated as missing. pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(result, df)

title: Check the source and audit missingness
text:
Analyze a real public dataset Begin a public-data analysis by identifying the source, version, and field definitions. A checksum can confirm that the local source file matches the recorded bytes, while a missingness audit tells you what is available to analyze. These checks do not prove that every scientific measurement is correct. import hashlib
folder = DATA_DIR / "public"
metadata = json.loads((folder / "provenance.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
digest = hashlib.sha256((folder / "penguins.csv").read_bytes()).hexdigest()
assert digest == metadata["artifacts"]["penguins.csv"]["sha256"]
df = pd.read_csv(folder / "penguins.csv", na_values=["NA"])
result = pd.DataFrame({"Missing": df.isna().sum(), "Known": df.notna().sum()})
print("Dataset:", metadata["dataset"])
print("Source commit:", metadata["upstream"]["commit"])
print("Shape:", df.shape)
print(result) Read the source into df. Store a dictionary named result with keys total_rows, rows_with_any_missing, complete_rows, and rows_with_known_mass. Calculate those four counts across the source fields without deleting rows from df. A row position is a way to trace the source file, not an animal identifier.

title: Choose exclusions to match the question
text:
Analyze a real public dataset A body-mass summary needs a known body mass and a grouping label. It does not automatically need recorded sex. Keep an exclusion audit and retain original units; this exercise does not replace missing measurements with invented values. df = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "public" / "penguins.csv", na_values=["NA"])
df.insert(0, "source_row", np.arange(1, len(df) + 1))
required = ["species", "body_mass_g"]
missing_required = df[required].isna().any(axis=1)
audit = df.loc[missing_required, ["source_row"] + required].copy()
result = df.loc[~missing_required].copy()
assert result["body_mass_g"].gt(0).all()
print("Rows retained:", len(result))
print("Excluded rows:")
print(audit)
print("Retained rows with unrecorded sex:", result["sex"].isna().sum()) Change the question to body-mass summaries by species and sex. Require species, sex, and body_mass_g. Recreate the retained result and exclusion audit from the original file; do not reuse the earlier filtered table. Report exclusions and consider whether the remaining observations differ systematically; these checks do not establish random missingness.

title: Report group means with their denominators
text:
Analyze a real public dataset A group mean uses the known measurements in that group. Show total observations, known measurements, and missing measurements beside the mean so readers can see its denominator. The summaries describe these observations; they do not establish causal species or island effects. df = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "public" / "penguins.csv", na_values=["NA"])
result = df.groupby("species", as_index=False).agg(Observations=("species", "size"), Known_mass=("body_mass_g", "count"), Mean_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean"))
result["Missing_mass"] = result["Observations"] - result["Known_mass"]
print(result.round({"Mean_mass_g": 2}))
print("Total observed records:", result["Observations"].sum())
print("Total known body masses:", result["Known_mass"].sum()) Group by island instead of species. Store result with island as a normal column, sorted in ascending island order, and report Observations, Known_mass, Missing_mass, and Mean_mass_g. Reconcile the total observations and known measurements with the full table. Sample sizes and species composition differ across islands. A descriptive comparison is not an adjusted causal analysis.

title: Create a chart and an auditable export

A chart can summarize the sampled measurements without claiming a population estimate or a causal finding. df = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "public" / "penguins.csv", na_values=["NA"])
result = df.groupby("species", as_index=False).agg(Observations=("species", "size"), Known_mass=("body_mass_g", "count"), Mean_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean"))
result["Missing_mass"] = result["Observations"] - result["Known_mass"]
result["Mean_mass_kg"] = result["Mean_mass_g"] / 1000
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ax.bar(result["species"], result["Mean_mass_kg"], color="#326f79")
for i, row in result.iterrows():
    ax.text(i, row["Mean_mass_kg"] + 0.08, f"n={int(row['Known_mass'])}", ha="center")
ax.set(title="Mean observed penguin body mass, 2007–2009", xlabel="Species", ylabel="Mean body mass (kg)", ylim=(0, 6))
fig.tight_layout()
csv_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "public_penguins_mass_summary.csv"
plot_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "public_penguins_mass_summary.png"
result.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
fig.savefig(plot_path, dpi=160)
print(result.round({"Mean_mass_g": 2, "Mean_mass_kg": 3}))
print("Source: Palmer Penguins; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3960218. Means use known body masses.")
print("These summaries describe sampled observations, not causal effects or a population census.")
